description.narrative:
HER VOICE, HER FUTURE is a youth-led advocacy initiative amplifying the voices of teenage mothers, young women with disabilities, and rural youth in Kapelebyong District. The project strengthens youth leadership and advocacy capacity, facilitates evidence-based policy dialogue with district leaders, and supports youth-led monitoring of maternal health and GBV services. Through community mobilisation, media engagement, and direct participation in governance spaces, the project connects grassroots realities to district, national, AU, and EU policy platforms. It advances meaningful youth participation, accountability, and alignment with AU Agenda 2063, enabling marginalised young women to transition from silence to leadership and influence over decisions shaping their rights and futures.
Goal: Strengthen youth-led advocacy for safe motherhood, GBV accountability, disability inclusion, and meaningful participation of marginalized youth.
Objectives: Build advocacy and leadership capacity of teenage mothers and young women with disabilities Increase youth participation in district planning and budgeting Improve accountability of maternal health and GBV services Activities: Advocacy training's; youth-led service scorecards; policy dialogues; inclusive community forums; radio and media advocacy; coalition building.

participating-org.narrative:
Wings and Wheels Foundation (WWF) is a youth-led, grassroots women’s rights and community development organization registered with Uganda’s NGO Bureau. WWF works at the intersection of safe motherhood, gender-based violence (GBV) prevention, disability inclusion,youth-responsive governance, and holistic community empowerment. Through feminist, rights-based advocacy, civic engagement, and social accountability, the organization empowers teenage mothers, out-of-school girls, rural young women, young womenwith disabilities,and girls heading households to claim their rights, monitor public services, and influence policies, plans, and budgets that affecttheir lives.
In addition to advocacy, WWF implements practical community programs including youth livelihoods and skilling for teen mothers, education support for child-headed households, climate-smart agriculture for extremely vulnerable households, improved rural housing, and access to safe water. To date, WWF has supported 120 child-headed households, enabling 60 children to access safe boarding education.
Vision: An inclusive, just, and equitable society where young women, teenage mothers, and vulnerable families realize their rights, dignity, leadership potential, and improved living conditions.
Mission: To empower marginalised young women andvulnerable communities through youth-led, feminist, rights-based advocacy and partnerships.
Objectives: Promote safe motherhood; prevent and respond to GBV; strengthen youth leadership and civic participation; advance disability inclusion; support child-headed households; and strengthen social accountability.
Core Values: Feminist leadership, human rights, inclusion, equity, accountability,solidarity, and empowerment.
